title: A Cheeky Check
transcript: Sometimes harmony beats brute force. In this position, the white king and the black king are facing each other. The white king has a rook and a knight, but black has a pretty active bishop and most importantly a full queen. So it might seem like white is completely lost in this position. But as I told you, harmony is fundamental here. And you might notice that the black king is almost surrounded by the king, pawns, and knight. Meaning that if we can somehow play the move knight E3 check, this is going to be checkmate. But unfortunately, black can simply capture that knight with the queen. But this means that white can afford to do crazy things just to try and distract the queen from this square. And that's where the idea rook to B7 comes from. We sacrifice an entire rook to the queen. But of course, if the rook is taken, this would be checkmate. So after rook to B7, the queen has to go to D4. This not only guards the knight check, but it also guards that rook check behind the king. Except it doesn't because remember all we want to achieve is this checkmate with the knight. So we can actually sacrifice the rook again. Now the smart board is showing us that the king is in check. So something has to be done. And unfortunately for black, if the king goes to F5, the only square available, this move is going to deliver a checkmate. meaning that black is left with no other choice but to capture this rook. But now this knight can deliver the fatal blow with knight to e3 checkmate. If you would like your own smartboard, you can get one from the link in bio with code P10 for a great discount.
